activities.caption: call the magnitude — the coordination bill
activities.name: soPathsEstimate

config.prompt: Communication paths grow as n(n−1)/2. At 100 people, roughly how many potential relationships must the structure carry?
config.why: 45 relationships at 10 people become 4,950 at 100 — no management fashion changes the arithmetic; structure replaces the hallway, deliberately or badly.
config.context: Doubling headcount more than doubles the coordination load.

activities.caption: file each new system under the boundary crossed
activities.name: soBoundaryBuckets

config.prompt: Each boundary crossed adds a management system. File them:
config.why: Going multinational adds qualitatively new work, not more of the old — and structure is a bet about which classification dimension will dominate the next decade.

activities.caption: pair each scale phenomenon with its record
activities.name: soScaleMatch

config.prompt: The economics of getting bigger — pair each with what the evidence says:

pairs.right: machines used more fully drive unit costs down
most deals fail to create acquirer value — integration is a communication problem wearing a finance costume
coordination costs, slow decisions, motivation decay

config.why: Bigger is not automatically cheaper: profitability and craft are choices, not functions of headcount.

activities.anchor: The model's five phases map onto real schedules
activities.caption: walk Greiner's ladder, crisis and cure together
activities.name: soGreinerOrder

config.prompt: Greiner's phases, each ending in a crisis with a structural cure — order them:
items: Leadership crisis — solved by hiring managers
Direction through hierarchy, ending in an autonomy crisis — solved by delegation
Decentralised divisions, ending in a control crisis — solved by coordination systems
Red tape — solved (where it is solved) by collaboration structures
config.why: Name the crisis you are in and the cure follows from the phase — which is why reorganisations cluster at predictable headcounts (roughly 30, 100, 300, 1,000 in the folklore).

activities.anchor: Legal form is the scaling wardrobe
activities.caption: pick the growth philosophy, wear the consequences
activities.name: soFormBranch

config.root: The firm is ready to grow beyond what the founders' capital can fund. Each route is a different growth philosophy — choose.

start.text: Which scaling route does the firm take?

choices.label: Franchise the brand
choices.feedback: Scaling with other people's capital — the McDonald's model.

choices.label: IPO as a public limited company
choices.feedback: Capital markets — at the price of disclosure, quarterly pressure and diluted control.

choices.label: Cooperative or employee ownership
choices.feedback: Mondragon's federation of co-ops and John Lewis are the existence proofs — ownership scaled without external shareholders.

franchise.text: The brand scales on franchisees' capital; quality control becomes the core management system.

ipo.text: New fiduciary duties, new reporting, new external voices — governance changed as much as finance.

coop.text: Motivation is bound to structure — tens of thousands of worker-owners in Mondragon's case.

config.why: The exit choice is itself organisational design: Patagonia's 2022 transfer to a trust declared, structurally, that the firm had finished scaling toward capital.

activities.caption: true or false — motivation at volume
activities.name: soMotivateJudge

statements.s: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction; motivators like achievement, recognition and growth create satisfaction.
statements.why: Herzberg's distinction scales surprisingly well as design guidance.

statements.s: Fix pay and conditions at market, then invest in the motivators at volume.
statements.why: Promotion clarity, meaningful work and recognition rituals are the motivators' scaling form.

statements.s: Equity's motivational delta strengthens as the company grows.
statements.why: Delta decays with company size and vesting horizons — mature firms lean on progression frameworks.

statements.s: Bonuses are the biggest part of the motivation system's announcement.
statements.why: What gets recognised and promoted IS the announcement — bonuses are the smallest part of it.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — where familiarity stops scaling
activities.name: soDunbarEstimate

config.prompt: Past roughly how many stable human relationships must structure carry what familiarity used to?
config.why: Dunbar's number — about 150 — is why sub-150-person firms can run on familiarity and larger ones cannot: past that line, structure must carry what relationships used to.
config.context: The first manager-of-managers transition is the hardest — the skills genuinely change.

activities.anchor: Google's internal research famously found structure beats impression
activities.caption: one line of the hiring-at-scale summary is wrong
activities.name: soHiringSpot

config.prompt: One line of this hiring-at-scale summary is wrong. Find it.
lines: At ten people, everyone interviews everyone on instinct
At a thousand, instinct compounds bias and noise
Structured interviews use the same questions, scoring rubrics and work-sample tests
Culture interviews guard values by testing affinity — do I like this person?
Promoting on demonstrated delegation scales management as fast as headcount
config.correction: Culture interviews guard values only if they test behaviours, not affinity.
config.why: Onboarding converts hiring spend into productivity instead of churn — and training managers to train managers is the compounding investment.
